scheme_name: Repair Renovation Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies
overview: The Repair Renovation Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies scheme is a centrally sponsored component under the Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY). It aims to restore and revive water bodies such as tanks, ponds, and lakes to enhance irrigation potential, improve water storage, recharge groundwater, and increase availability of drinking water. The scheme supports states in undertaking repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies with central financial assistance, particularly focusing on special category areas and drought-prone regions.
objectives: Restore and revive water bodies to enhance irrigation potential
Improve water storage capacity in tanks and ponds
Recharge groundwater through water body restoration
Increase availability of drinking water in rural areas
Expand cultivable area under assured irrigation
Improve on-farm water use efficiency and promote water conservation
Support special category areas including drought-prone, flood-prone, and tribal regions
Strengthen water security through community-based water management
eligibility: State governments are eligible to propose projects under the RRR of Water Bodies scheme. Projects must focus on repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies such as tanks, ponds, and lakes. Priority is given to special category areas including drought-prone (DPAP), tribal, flood-prone, Left-Wing extremist dominated areas (e.g., Koraput, Bolangir, Kalahandi districts of Odisha), Bundelkhand region of UP and MP, and Marathwada & Vidarbha region of Maharashtra. The scheme is implemented under the Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY).
benefits: Financial assistance from the central government for repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies. Non-financial benefits include increased irrigation potential, improved groundwater recharge, enhanced drinking water availability, better water use efficiency, and stabilization of irrigation through revived water bodies. The scheme supports sustainable water management and contributes to drought resilience and climate adaptation in rural areas.
financial_support: Under the RRR of Water Bodies scheme, the Government of India provides central financial assistance to state governments for undertaking repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies. The funding pattern is based on project categories and follows the guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY). Central assistance is released in instalments based on project progress and utilization certificates. The scheme operates as a centrally sponsored scheme with cost-sharing between the Centre and states as per PMKSY norms.
application_process: 1. State governments identify water bodies requiring repair, renovation, and restoration. 2. Project proposals are prepared with detailed project reports (DPRs) including scope, cost estimates, and expected benefits. 3. Proposals are submitted to the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation (DoWR, RD & GR) for appraisal. 4. The DoWR, RD & GR appraises the proposals for technical feasibility and alignment with scheme objectives. 5. Upon approval, central assistance is sanctioned and released in instalments. 6. State governments implement the projects through concerned departments or agencies. 7. Progress is monitored through periodic reporting and field inspections. 8. Utilization certificates and completion reports are submitted for final settlement.
required_documents: Environmental and social impact assessment (if applicable)
Undertaking from state government for operation and maintenance
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per the financial year cycle.
implementing_agency: Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation (DoWR, RD & GR), Ministry of Jal Shakti
caveats: Central assistance is subject to availability of funds and adherence to scheme guidelines
Projects must be completed within the stipulated timeline; delays may affect fund release
Benefits are contingent upon proper operation and maintenance of restored water bodies by state governments or local bodies
Priority is given to special category areas; general areas may receive lower allocation
Submission of utilization certificates and progress reports is mandatory for subsequent fund releases
